proposition.claim:
Equation reference: eq:nash, eq:weight. For quadratic Hamiltonians, the backward system is \[
-\partial_t u^i-\operatorname{tr}\bigl((\sigma I+\beta J)D^2u^i\bigr)
+\frac12|D_i u^i|^2+\sum_{j\ne i}D_j u^j\cdot D_j u^i=f^i,
\qquad u^i(T,\cdot)=g^i.\] Here \(J=J_N\otimes I_d\), \(\sigma>0,\beta\ge0\). The paper uses Euclidean vector norms and quadratic-form matrix order even for nonsymmetric matrices. Its distinguished weighted norm is \[
\|x\|_i^2=|x^i|^2+\frac1N\sum_{j\ne i}|x^j|^2.\] The mean-field conditions (MF) control own-state and off-diagonal derivatives with different powers of \(N\); they do not uniformly bound the full Frobenius norm of a diagonal matrix.

The \(\mathcal D\)-condition controls the one-sided Lipschitz constant of \(x\mapsto(D_i h^i(x))_i\). The \(\mathcal L\)-condition concerns sums of four-point rectangular differences. Neither supplies symmetry of the mixed Jacobian. Theorems 3.8 and A.1 require small semimonotonicity constants and large \(N\), with additional convexity hypotheses for general Hamiltonians. The heterogeneous limit requires bounded smooth data, symmetry in other players’ states, and label regularity (LP). Section 7 sets \(\sigma=1,\beta=0\); Section 8 instead takes \(\sigma=\sigma_N\downarrow0\) with a lower bound on \(\sigma_N\log\log N\).

The principal dependency requiring further work is the application of Lemma 4.3 in Proposition 8.1 to obtain a gradient bound independent of \(N\) and \(\sigma_N\). Problems 1 and 2 concern different aspects of that argument and its statement. The remaining problems have more local repair boundaries.

repair.content:
Supply a genuine game-specific weighted gradient estimate, or prove an appropriate weighted one-sided bound for the actual drift. Merely checking the forcing term (4.3), as on p69, is insufficient. No full replacement proof is certified.

Replace D_x F(x_i,m_y^-i) by D_x F(y_i,m_y^-i), likewise for G, and state explicitly that the smallness concerns Definition 3.1. This removes this counterexample but does not resolve P001.

Use C(|Delta lambda_1|+N^-1 sum_{j>1}|Delta lambda_j|), or its l2/sqrt(N) consequence. Restore the terminal derivative contribution in the short-interval estimate and justify the componentwise gradient estimate before iteration. A complete replacement gradient proof is not claimed.

Add C|lambda-lambda'| to (7.25), propagate it through the drift comparison, and reverse the mixed diffusion sign. Direct synchronous stochastic coupling proves the corrected estimate.

Replace the maximum-position bound by the proved common-mass average-moment bound, including label distance. Use bounded-drift individual/group average moments to pass to expectation.

Conclude only that the symmetric off-diagonal part vanishes; drop the false reverse equivalence. Bound the diagonal part in operator norm and the off-diagonal part by its Frobenius norm: ||J||op<=2Lg, giving Cg^2<=4Lg^2 (and similarly for f).

Correct the forward drift and running-cost signs; include ||H(.,0)^+||infinity as well as the negative lower bound of H in the value estimate. Use the matrix kernel or its correct eigenvalue expansion and correct Duhamel times. These are local formula repairs, not a replacement proof of all external Schauder inputs.

Add separability of Gamma (sufficient here) and give the dense-set diagonal argument.
